items.stem: According to the hierarchy of controls, which option is most effective at reducing a hazard?

options.rationale: Correct: elimination is the most effective control because it removes the hazard entirely.
PPE is the least effective control, used last.
Administrative controls rank below engineering controls.
Warnings are administrative controls, low on the hierarchy.

items.explanation: Elimination is the most effective control in the hierarchy.

items.stem: Which of the following is a leading safety indicator?

options.rationale: Correct: completed inspections are a proactive, leading indicator.
TRIR is a lagging indicator, measured after incidents occur.
Comp cost is a lagging financial outcome.

items.explanation: Completed inspections are a leading indicator; the others are lagging.

items.stem: A risk assessment rates risk from severity and likelihood. Select TWO actions that correctly lower the assessed risk level.

options.text: Install engineering controls that reduce the severity of a release
options.rationale: Correct: reducing severity lowers the risk score.

options.text: Reduce exposure frequency to lower likelihood
options.rationale: Correct: reducing likelihood lowers the risk score.

options.text: Rename the hazard category in the register
options.rationale: Relabelling does not change actual risk.

options.text: Increase the number of warning signs only
options.rationale: Signs are weak controls and change risk little.

options.text: Remove the hazard from the register without action
options.rationale: Deleting a record hides risk rather than reducing it.

items.explanation: Lowering severity and likelihood both reduce assessed risk; relabelling or hiding does not.
